fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Ceiling That Already Holds a Horoscope", "body": "The test case is the Sala di Galatea in Rome's Villa Farnesina, the vaulted loggia attributed to Baldassare Peruzzi around 1510 and 1511, where mainstream historians already read a horoscope for the villa's builder, the banker Agostino Chigi, whose baptismal record from Siena gives a birth on November 29, 1466. In his 2019 book Roxolana, Anatoly Fomenko argues the same vault actually encodes December 31, 1656, which would mean any challenger must not only reread the painted sky but also dismiss a surviving paper trail as forgery."}, {"title": "Phantom Duplicates and a Pope's Rewritten Family", "body": "Fomenko contends that the famous Renaissance banker is merely a phantom reflection of a later Agostino Chigi, the nephew of Fabio Chigi, who reigned as Pope Alexander VII and, in his telling, steered a family rewrite of Italian history that slid events 150 to 200 years into the past, turning Carlo Maratta's frescoes into Raphael's. Chance counters that a powerful family naming a son after its most celebrated forefather is hardly suspicious, notes that portraits Fomenko said he could not find sat on Wikipedia years before his book, and stresses that every downstream claim hangs on one disputed date."}, {"title": "Reading the Zodiac Panel by Panel", "body": "Walking the ten hexagonal panels from Aries to Pisces, Chance matches each figure to a planet or a constellation myth: Jupiter's bull garlanded by Europa from Ovid's Metamorphoses, Leda and her swan for Gemini, Hercules and the crab for Cancer, Erigone and her faithful dog for a Virgo moon, Mars and Mercury beside the scales and scorpion. Fomenko, by contrast, recasts the swan as the moon to manufacture a lunar eclipse, swaps Erigone for Procris while excusing the very missing details he holds against her, and reads Saturn's sheaf of grain as Spica, scattering the signs out of their painted order."}, {"title": "Tropical, Sidereal, and a Five Degree Cushion", "body": "Because Fomenko keeps the sun in Sagittarius for a December 31 date, his chart only works on a sidereal reckoning built from unequal constellation divisions plus a self granted five degree tolerance, a system Chance could not reproduce on any mainstream astrology site and could find no sign of among Renaissance Italians, who cast charts tropically. Dylan explains why the tropical frame tracks the seasons while precession drifts the stars. Running both readings through the Swiss Ephemeris, Chance found the conventional placements, with Mars read in Scorpio, land on November 29, 1466, while Fomenko's date never matched cleanly."}, {"title": "Selective Skepticism and the Faith of Truthers", "body": "The hosts frame Fomenko's habit as heads I win, tails you lose: evidence that fits is reliable, while a baptismal record that contradicts him becomes forgery, the same selective skepticism they see in Tartaria and old world reset videos that unknowingly post their own rebuttals, like the Florentine picture chronicle on Fomenko's own website naming the grain as Saturn's emblem. Replacing a lie with a lie leaves nobody better off, they argue, and astronomical dating itself, practiced long before Nikolai Morozov, remains a sound method; it is Fomenko's interpretations, not the idea, that collapse under replication."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Does a Renaissance painting contain evidence that nearly 200 years of history were invented? Chance Garton and Dylan Saccoccio investigate Anatoly Fomenko's New Chronology through the zodiac ceiling of the Sala di Galatea at Rome's Villa Farnesina. The conventional interpretation connects the ceiling's horoscope to Agostino Chigi's birth in 1466, while Fomenko proposes 1656, and that difference leads to much bigger claims: phantom duplicates of historical figures, a powerful pope's family rewriting Italian history, and works attributed to Raphael being reassigned to Carlo Maratta.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In Inner Whirled 32, we examine the artwork panel by panel, compare interpretations of its mythological and planetary symbolism, and check the proposed dates against the sky. What do the sources support? Which planetary placements can we reproduce? And how much depends on the assumptions behind the reading? Whether you support New Chronology or question its conclusions, follow the investigation and examine the evidence with us.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Fomenko Turns the Venus and Mary Myth Backwards", "body": "Fomenko accepts the Venus in Capricorn panel, but digresses into a claim that Venus is a reflection of the Virgin Mary. Chance lays out the reversal: Inner Whirled has argued that Mary grows out of the older myths of Venus and Aphrodite, while Fomenko says Venus and Aphrodite are based on a historical Mary of the Middle Ages. Dylan agrees the panel ties Venus to Mary, reading it through Virgo Marina, the Virgin of the Sea, who rules the night sky from midnight as the sun enters Capricorn. Chance also flags that Fomenko presents Galatea as meaning a Galatian woman as if it were established fact, when it is not."}, {"title": "Galich, Seashells and a Russian Princess", "body": "Reading on, Fomenko places the Mother of God in Galich in the Kostroma region and ties both Galatia and Paul's Galatians to that town. He claims the seashell of Venus preserves the impression a golden haired, blue eyed Russian princess made on twelfth century Constantinople, and offers shell framed Marian reliefs from Milan Cathedral as support. The hosts point to his hedging, where each probably and most likely quietly hardens into certainty by the conclusion. They grant that the shell genuinely links Venus to Mary, but the Bible places Mary in Galilee, and Chance finds only Orthodox legends bringing her to Galatia after the crucifixion."}, {"title": "Galatea, Venus and Mary as One Goddess", "body": "Chance builds a nine point case that Galatea, Venus and Mary rest on the same astrotheology. Each is tied to the sea, marked by whiteness and milk, bound to a beloved young man who dies violently and is transformed, and honored as a mother of nations. Acis becomes a spring, Adonis becomes a flower, and blood and water flow at the crucifixion, while Macrobius reads Adonis as the sun mourned through winter. Chance grants Fomenko the association but rejects the Russian princess, adding that New Chronology identifies Jesus with the Byzantine emperor Andronikos I, so citing Fomenko in support of Millennial Reign beliefs undercuts itself."}, {"title": "Saturn's Wheat and the Harvest Tradition", "body": "Fomenko reads the wheat in Saturn's hand as Spica, placing Saturn retrograde in Virgo. Chance counters that Saturn holding grain never meant Spica, since Roman folklore preserved in the Saturnalia of Macrobius credits Saturn with teaching agriculture, and an 1880 handbook, Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome, describes him bearing a sickle and a wheat sheaf. Fomenko sidesteps this by arguing that a harvest attribute implies autumn while his sidereal Sagittarius sun means winter, yet he never applies that logic to Jupiter's thunderbolt or the armor of Mars. A Masonic emblem, Saturn and the Weeping Virgin, carries the same theme of mourning the sun."}, {"title": "Logical Traps and a Date Nobody Explains", "body": "In the two central ceiling panels, which Chance reads as northern constellations such as Perseus and Ursa Major, Fomenko finds another horoscope, casting Perseus as Mars, Medusa as the sun and Fama as the moon. That gives one ceiling three dates, 1622, 1656 and 1658, yet Chance notes Fomenko never explains 1622, and the later Agostino Chigi was not born until 1634. In Roxolana, Fomenko warns of deliberate logical traps for inexperienced viewers while calling his own reading clear, a double standard the hosts dissect. Chance's takeaway is that technical density can hide arbitrary choices, so listeners should check everyone's work, including theirs."}]

So she's like the queen of the night sky, if you will, queen of heaven.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Being suspicious of something, that's not the problem. Saturn and Virgo are different things entirely.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "What blows my mind is that this date 1622 that he says is encoded in these center panels, he never explains what that date is for.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Be wary. With us, too. We want you to check our work. We try to show you our work as we go to help with this problem.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Technical density of information can conceal interpretations that are just arbitrary choices.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Just because you can point out one thing is wrong or incorrectly dated or fraud, that doesn't give you the right to then fill in the void of what actually did happen.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "We have almost nothing interesting of value regarding written works from the ancient Roman Empire and the ancient Etruscan Empire and all that stuff. And it's very suspicious to me.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "What makes our analysis on this show different is that we're completely skeptical of replacement ideas from truthers too. Because if you replace a lie with a lie, are you any better off?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "What's more likely, a powerful family would name a son after a famous forefather, or that there's two Agostino Chigis in history, therefore one is a fake duplication?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "There's no myths about Leda, this queen, being the earth. There's no myths about the swan that impregnates her being the moon. None of that exists.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Fomenko accepts all of those just fine, except the ones he needs to be different. And then he makes giant leaps of logic without support.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "All this stuff is just man's way of trying to keep track of an imperfect system that doesn't precisely correspond with the mathematical concepts that they've created to measure it.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "This is exactly what we've seen in the Tartaria videos all the time. They themselves put forward the evidence that debunks their idea and they don't even know that they did it.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The fact that I could not find a way to match his version of the calculation using modern astrology websites means that it's a unique method of calculating the sky to him.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "This is what Fomenko does. Anything that he can twist to support himself, he says it's reliable. Anything that breaks his theory, he says it's a forgery.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I have gone through so much and I have yet to find one detail emerging from the twelve hundreds of any of these things that would have led up to the empire of Tartaria.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "When you all offer an alternative that is not founded on anything, that's where you get in trouble.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
